# Edition Assembly

## Purpose

Turn a set of reviewed pages into something a reader can open. An edition is
a written list of the exact render that ships for every page, plus the files
exported from that list. Because the list names versions, anyone can tell
later which drawing went out, and because exports are never overwritten, an
earlier edition stays what it was.

## Use When

- Every page of an issue has a reviewed render and `/build-edition` runs.
- A reading copy of unfinished work is needed and a draft build will do.
- A page was repaired after publication and a corrected edition is due.
- The project lists a social carousel or a print deliverable and someone has
  to say what that involves.

## Inputs

- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/issue.yaml` and every `page.yaml` of the
  issue: `number`, `status`, `current_render`.
- The review file of each page's current render
  (`reviews/<RENDER_ID>.review.yaml`): `verdict` and `human_approval`.
- `production/project.yaml`: `title`, `comic_format`, `reading_direction`,
  `lettering.mode`, the `page` block, and `deliverables`.
- `production/continuity/<ISS_ID>.final-state.yaml`.
- Existing editions under `production/editions/`, for the next free ID and
  for `supersedes`.
- `rules/publishing/` and the project's format layer.

## Process

1. Check that the issue is ready. Every page has a `current_render`, and the
   review of that render has verdict `pass` or `fixed`. The continuity state
   for the issue exists. If any page falls short, either stop or build a
   draft and say so.
2. Take the next edition ID for the issue (`ED_<issue>_##`). Never reuse an
   ID, including for a build that failed.
3. Write `production/editions/<ED_ID>/edition.yaml`: `id`, `issue`, `title`,
   `label`, `status: draft`, `supersedes`, `changes`, `pages`, and an empty
   `exports` list.
4. List the pages in page-number order, once each, with no gaps. For every
   page set `render` to the exact render ID that ships and `file` to its
   path relative to the workspace root. Copy the ID from the page's
   `current_render` after confirming its review. Do not pick the newest
   file in `renders/`. It may be a rejected attempt.
5. Overlay lettering: for each page run
   `node scripts/letter-pages.js --page <page.yaml> --render <RENDER_ID>`,
   flatten the SVG over the render with a browser or a vector tool, and set
   `lettered_file` to the flattened image. It has to be a PNG or JPEG whose
   file name starts with the render ID (`<RENDER_ID>.lettered.png`); the
   build rejects an SVG. In `in_image` mode leave `lettered_file` as
   `null`.
6. Validate before building:
   `node scripts/validate-workspace.js --root <workspace> --issue <ISS_ID>`.
7. Build:
   `node scripts/build-edition.js --edition <edition.yaml> --formats pdf,cbz,web`.
   The script refuses an edition that lists a render without a `pass` or
   `fixed` review. For a reading copy of work in progress add `--draft`,
   which marks every export as a draft. The script does not overwrite an
   existing export. Leave `--force` for a build you are rerunning before
   anyone has received the files: it works only while the edition's status
   is `draft` or the build is `--draft`, and the script refuses it on a
   `reviewed` or `published` edition (`force-not-draft`).
8. Open every export. Count the pages, read them in order, and confirm that
   each page is the listed render. In the PDF check the page size. In the
   CBZ check that the files sort in reading order. In the web reader check
   that it advances in the project's `reading_direction`, or scrolls as one
   column for a webtoon.
9. Confirm that `exports` in `edition.yaml` lists each file with its
   `format`, `file`, and `built_at`.
10. Move the status on evidence. `draft` becomes `reviewed` when the exports
    have been opened and checked. `reviewed` becomes `published` when the
    user says the edition has gone out. A draft build never becomes
    `published`.
11. Correct by superseding. When a published page changes, create a new
    edition with the next ID, set `supersedes` to the old one, and list in
    `changes` which page now uses which render and why. Leave the old
    edition's directory untouched.
12. Handle the other deliverables listed in `project.yaml`. For
    `social-carousel`, name the pages or panels to post and the crop each
    needs. For `print`, state the trim, bleed, and safe margin from the
    `page` block and what the printer requires. Record both as notes on the
    edition and hand them to a person or an image tool.

## Outputs

- `production/editions/<ED_ID>/edition.yaml` (`edition.schema.json`).
- Exports under `production/editions/<ED_ID>/exports/`: PDF, CBZ, and a web
  reader, named `<title-slug>-<issue number>-ed<edition number>[-DRAFT]`
  with `.pdf`, `.cbz`, or the directory suffix `-web`
  (`the-night-ferry-001-ed01.cbz`).
- Overlay mode: lettered page files referenced by `lettered_file`.
- A delivery note: the current render of every page by filename, what was
  repaired since the last edition, what was visually rechecked, and what
  still needs a decision.

## Quality Bar

- Every page of the issue appears once, in page-number order, with an
  explicit render ID and a file that exists.
- In a non-draft edition, every listed render has a review with verdict
  `pass` or `fixed`.
- No export file from an earlier build or an earlier edition was replaced.
- A corrected edition has a new ID, a `supersedes` value, and a non-empty
  `changes` list.
- Each export was opened and its page count matches `page_count` in
  `issue.yaml`.
- The delivery note does not call a draft or a flagged page approved.

## Common Failure Modes

- Building from whatever file is newest in `renders/`, which ships a
  rejected attempt.
- Rebuilding into the same edition after a repair, so two people hold
  different files with the same name.
- A flagged page slipped into a reviewed edition because the build ran with
  `--draft` and the status was changed afterwards.
- Pages out of order or one missing, found by a reader.
- Overlay lettering left as an SVG beside the art, and the exported page has
  no text.
- An `rtl` book exported with a left-to-right web reader.
- Rejected renders deleted to tidy up, which removes the evidence for the
  reviews.
- A carousel promised as an automatic output.

## Notes

What the scaffold automates: checking the edition against the reviews,
assembling the listed images into PDF, CBZ, and a web reader, and refusing
to overwrite. What it leaves to other tools: flattening lettering overlays
into raster images, cropping or resizing pages for a social carousel, and
preparing print files with bleed, trim marks, or color conversion. The
edition records those deliverables and their specifications. It does not
produce them.

Keep every render and every review on disk after the edition ships. They
are the record of why each listed version was chosen.
